title: Dessau Grid — Bauhaus Primary Crit
description: A strict 12-column grid anchors oversized primary-color primitives — red square, cobalt circle, cadmium triangle — set in all-caps geometric-sans type with generous tracking. Where other Bauhaus-adjacent templates merely reference the movement, this one enacts its logic.
philosophy: This template exists to make the argument through its own structure: the tension between a playful 40%-scale primitive and a relentless ink-black grid is the lecture. It draws directly from Bayer's universal letterform discipline and Vkhutemas workshop pedagogy, treating ornament not as optional but as categorically wrong. The speaker using it knows why the shapes collide and can defend every alignment decision. Gradients, rounded corners, and decorative rules are not suppressed here — they are simply outside the vocabulary this system recognizes.
goodFor: Design-history lectures on Bauhaus, Constructivism, and De Stijl
Typography studio critiques and concept-defense presentations
3-line pull quotes anchored over a large single-color geometric field
Brand identity workshops framed within a modernist design canon
avoidFor: Chart-heavy quarterly business reviews requiring data density
Warm lifestyle, wellness, or consumer brand pitches
Presentations needing more than five distinct hues to function
Dense academic papers where body-text legibility outweighs structural drama
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide opens like a manifesto pinned to a Bauhaus workshop wall — declarative, compressed, with zero deference to comfort. A single massive primary-colored geometric shape claims the right half of the frame not as illustration but as structural argument, its hard edge colliding against the invisible grid that disciplines the left. The composition is deliberately pressured on one side and cold-open on the other, enacting asymmetric balance through arithmetic rather than intuition. Nothing softens, nothing curves; every element defends its position by logic alone.

examples.layoutNotes: The strict 12-column grid governs all placement: a single oversized geometric primitive — the red square — bleeds from the right edge, occupying columns 8–12 and filling roughly 40% of the slide height, hard-cropped at the top and right bleed. Title text sits all-caps in columns 1–7, vertically locked to the upper third of the slide; subtitle occupies the same column band one full grid row below. A hairline ink-black horizontal rule spans columns 1–5 beneath the subtitle block, acting as the sole separating device. Deck identifier or course code sits flush-left at the bottom margin within columns 1–2 — no footer band, no centered anything.

examples.promptCore: The slide stages a Bauhaus workshop critique in visual form: one oversized, unmodulated primary-color primitive bleeds off the left edge — raw, flat, and unapologetic — while the right zone locks tightly tracked all-caps text into strict vertical rhythm against the black grid. The mood is pedagogical and confrontational; every element earns its coordinates or is absent entirely. Compositionally asymmetric but never accidental: the shape's blunt mass is held in tension by the compressed discipline of the typographic block opposite it. Avoid all softening impulses — no transitional gradients, no friendly rounded forms, no decorative hospitality of any kind.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with a single oversized flat geometric primitive (circle or square) bleeding off the left slide edge and occupying roughly the leftmost third of the canvas — no margin, hard crop. Text content (a 3-line pull quote, stacked feature list, or stat callout) is set in cols 5–11 with an 8% right outer margin. A hairline-weight horizontal rule separates a short all-caps category label from the body text block at the top of the text zone. Slide number sits bottom-right, flush to the grid edge with no surrounding frame.
